title: Model variant compatibility checks and graceful fallback policy for staged rollouts
creator: Marco Alvarez
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility checker run on every model-pack push and returns pass/fail with explicit incompatible fields
Canary engine can route shadow traffic to a candidate variant without impacting production QPS
Automated auto-rollback triggers on sustained error rate delta > 0.5% for 3 minutes or p95 latency regression > 15%
Region failover policy documented and exercised in chaos test (post-deploy smoke)
testing_plan: Unit tests for compatibility validator (tokenizer mismatch, KV shape, kv-cache retention flags)
Integration tests: simulate mixed-version KV cache accesses and verify fallback to stateless path
Load test: 30m at 2x typical traffic with 10% canary weight, measure tail latency & error rate
Chaos run: kill primary region, confirm routing to standby region within target failover window
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Shadow run for 24h at 0% traffic (mirror) to collect output diffs and perf metrics
Phase 1: Canary 5% for 1h, automated health checks (latency p95, error rate, token cost)
Phase 2: Canary 20% for 3h if Phase 1 OK, run A/B quality evals tied to prompt sets
Phase 3: Ramp to 100% with circuit-breaker gating and ability to route to quantized fallback variant
Rollback: Automatic rollback to previous pinned model if any rule fires; manual rollback option for infra team
body:
Purpose:
Implement a model-variant compatibility checker and a composable routing + fallback policy to support staged rollouts (shadow, canary, A/B) with safe auto-rollback and region-aware failover. This ticket focuses on the runtime-side checks and the decisions for graceful degradation when a candidate model or model variant is incompatible or causes regressions.

Background and motivation:
We continue to see rollout-related incidents where a model variant (different tokenizer, quantized weights, or modified KV layout) would succeed locally but cause cache misses, longer decode loops, or subtle errors in production. In addition, we need deterministic behavior when primary regions are overloaded or when Dedicated capacity is constrained. Our goal is to make rollouts predictable and to minimize blast radius by:
- catching incompatibilities early (pre-deploy and at deploy-time),
- providing shadow / mirror runs to compare outputs without exposing users,
- implementing staged weight ramps with A/B metrics and quality gates,
- falling back to compatible model variants or alternate regions when thresholds are breached.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
1) Strict pre-deploy gating vs best-effort runtime compatibility: we will enforce a compatibility validator that can block deploys for critical mismatches (tokenizer vocab, embedding dim mismatch) and allow non-blocking warnings for perf-affecting changes (slightly different kv ordering). This balances speed for model engineers and safety for production.
2) Auto-rollback sensitivity: conservative triggers (short window) reduce exposure but increase false rollbacks on transient infra noise. Chosen default: sustained violation for 3 minutes with rolling window checks and evidence from both error-rate and latency deltas before triggering auto-rollback.
3) Fallback variants: prefer functional compatibility over model fidelity — we will route to a quantized-but-compatible variant when candidate fails performance SLOs, and to previous pinned model on correctness/quality regressions.

Compatibility checks implemented in this ticket:
- Tokenizer fingerprint check (vocab hash + special token mapping)
- Model signature: expected input dims, output dims, embeddings size, kv-cache shape version
- Feature flags compatibility (streaming/structured-output hooks, function calling hooks)
- Quantization profile compatibility: ensure runtime supports requested quant format (int8, nf4)
- Soft checks: parameter count and attention layout differences reported as warnings

Routing & policy rules to be added to runtime: 
- Route type support: stable -> candidate split by percentage, shadow mirror copies of requests, A/B sticky routing by user-id for multi-hour experiments
- Fallback chain: candidate -> quantized-variant -> pinned-previous-model -> region-staging -> global-fallback (smaller model)
- Tiered capacity fallback: when Dedicated pool saturates, route Excess requests to cheaper shared pool but with lower throughput guarantees; any overflow beyond shared pool triggers rate-limited 503s with graceful degradation header
- Region failover: preference order per customer: same-region -> nearest-region -> cross-region fallback; on failover, respect data residency labels and only fallback to allowed regions

Observability and debugging hooks:
- model-compatibility-dashboard (Grafana) with counters for each check and per-deploy heatmap
- per-request fingerprint logs for failed requests with correlation-id forwarded to trace
- automated snapshot diff storage for shadow runs (store 24h) and an eval scorecard to track quality drift

Implementation notes & work completed so far:
- Compatibility validator library prototype added to runtime repo (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5283) — unit tests added for tokenizer fingerprinting
- Shadow routing plumbing implemented in staging, uses mirror queue and separate telemetry path (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/312)
- Canary weight gating implemented in router service; simple percentage ramps wired to rollout service (internal flag settable per-deploy)
- Initial Grafana dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/model-compatibility-dashboard

Open work & blockers:
- Integration tests with Dedicated pool autoscaling hooks (ENG-6011) need to be merged before canary at scale
- Region-residency policy engine needs decision from Legal for EU->APAC fallback allowances (request submitted to Legal on 2026-03-02)
- Finalize the human-override UI in Console for pausing auto-rollback (Design input: DES-2043)

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Finish integration tests and add chaos scenario for region failover (owner: Linh) — target 2026-03-18
- Add A/B evaluation artifacts: prompt sets and scoring functions (owner: Aisha)
- Run internal canary with non-critical tenant group for 48h shadow -> 5% -> 20% (owner: Marco)

Related links and artifacts:
- Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Runtime+Fallback+and+Rollout+Patterns
- PR for compatibility library: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5283
- Routing changes PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/312
- Evaluation harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/commit/ab3f5f

Risk assessment:
- Medium: if compatibility checks miss a case, we risk partial correctness regressions that may not surface in shadow runs. Mitigation: expand prompt set diversity and keep short retention snapshots to iterate quickly.

Owner notes: feel free to review the PRs and dashboards. The validator intentionally errs on the side of blocking for tokenizer/embedding mismatches; other checks are warnings that we can tune in the first month after launch.
